text:
dwight: idea: move away from per-prefix churn by grouping prefixes into short-lived cohorts. cohorts tracked by a time-decayed sketch (approx frequency + recency). eviction + demotion decisions operate at cohort granularity, with per-prefix soft-decay inside a cohort.
ana: sketch pls. how do cohorts get formed? based on prefix hash neighbourhood or semantic similarity?
dwight: initial plan: start simple: hash-prefix bucketing (configurable bits) + periodic merge if co-occurrence/cross-hit rate is high. later we can evaluate embedding-based grouping.
mike: important: RA-write semantics must be preserved. pinned prefixes should never join cohort demotion. plus we need an easy escape hatch for critical low-latency paths.
devon: what happens when a cohort is demoted but some members are still hot? we need intra-cohort prioritization. propose per-prefix score = cohort_score * local_decay_factor; eviction orders by that.
kari: also ops: how to store cohort metadata? small in-memory manifest per node? or global placement service?
dwight: manifest per shard with periodic sync. manifest: {cohort_id, epoch, bucket_bits, created_at, hotness_score}. keep tiny. prefer local authoritative per-shard to avoid global locking.
sasha: ops concern: metadata churn + manifest sync can add load. we should version manifests and apply delta updates: add/remove cohort entries only.
nana: correctness: cohort reassignments could cause stale reads if writers and readers disagree. we need a short-lived forward map: prefix -> (cohort_id, epoch) and a tombstone remap for transitions.
devon: prefer forwarded remap kept as in-memory small hash with epoch. flow: lookup prefix -> direct store hit. on miss consult remap; remap has TTL (e.g., 30s) and monotonic epoch to avoid cycles.
mike: that keeps common-path cheap. ensure remap is read-optimized: lock-free lookups (atomic pointer/word). on write commit we update remap with CAS.
kari: GC: how long to keep remaps? if we have long-lived leases, GC needs to wait for lease refcount or wall-time threshold. propose: max(lease_timeout+5s, 60s).
dwight: another safety: implement a circuit-breaker that monitors cohort-path p99 lookup delta. if cohort-lookup p99 > baseline + 1ms or tombstone rate > 0.5%, auto-disable cohort routing for that shard.
sasha: love the breaker. add metric for remap-bounce-rate (lookups that hit remap then main store) and cohort-split-frequency.
nana: on storage formats: when cohort is "cooled" we can move members to compressed resident (delta-encoded or 8-bit quantized) before full eviction. that reduces cold-reload cost.
devon: quantization options differ by deployment. default 8-bit in Hosted; Dedicated/Private can opt-in 4-bit tested paths. conversions async with fallback path to decompress on miss.
mike: key encoding question: do we change on-wire key to include cohort_id? i'd rather keep on-wire stable. keep cohort-index separate: prefix-hash -> cohort_id table local to node.
dwight: agreed. cohort-index is tiny and memory-first. implement as robin-hood hash table with aging.
kari: how to handle multi-tenant sharing? default: per-tenant cohort space. optional: co-tenant shared cohorts for customers that opt-in (mirror-index + tenant tag). must be explicit config.
nana: test plan: 1) offline sim on 90 days traces with cohort bucket sizes and decay params sweep. 2) small canary (0.5%) with cohort routing enabled read-only + metric collection. 3) active canary (1-2%) with full logic + circuit-breakers. 4) ramp.
devon: add chaos tests: random cohort merges/splits during high concurrency writes and ensure RA-write invariants for pinned keys.
sasha: dashboards: cohort_hit_rate, cohort_evicts/sec, remap_bounce_rate, cohort_reactivate_count, cohort_manifest_change_rate, circuit_breaker_trips.
mike: rollout guard: feature-flagged per-shard. default off for legacy clusters. auto-rollback if p99 delta > threshold for N minutes.
dwight: open implementation notes: - simple cohortizer = low bits of prefix-hash (configurable) - merge if co-hit rate > 60% for 5m window - split if internal skew: top 5% prefixes account for > 80% of cohort hits -> split into two cohorts.
nana: split logic important to avoid "monolith cohorts" that cause tail latencies. also add per-cohort LRU for intra-cohort fairness.
kari: concurrency details: update manifest via compare-and-swap on manifest version. manifest includes epoch; readers check epoch on lookup and follow remap if mismatch.
devon: also consider a lightweight per-request cache of cohort-index to avoid index lookup thrash for hot prefixes. TTL ~200ms.
sasha: deploy-bot: canary 2026-03-20-kv-cohort-run active in us-east-1 (no user impact).
mike: next steps: dwight to author RFC with pseudocode for manifest ops, remap lifetime, split/merge thresholds, and circuit-breaker criteria. include simulation results.
dwight: will draft. volunteers to validate sim traces?
devon: i'll run sim on chat dataset and share numbers by Tue.
kari: i'll scope dashboard tiles.
nana: i'll review RFC + test cases.
infra-bot: issue created KV-4720: "cohort-evict: RFC + canary plan" assigned to dwight.
dwight: thanks! please add any corner cases here. small ask: someone to baseline current miss/eviction churn this week?
devon: taking baseline.
mike: great, thanks all. :rocket:
